Paper: PARLOMA – A Novel Human-Robot Interaction System for Deaf-Blind Remote Communication
Venue: International Journal of Advanced Robotic Systems
System / Method: PARLOMA: depth sensing, networked ROS components and robotic hand
Capability Awareness?: Hardware abstraction; not negotiated user profile
Major Findings: Demonstrates remote reproduction of recognized hand shapes.
Limitations: Restricted hand-shape vocabulary; not general sign-language translation.
Relevance to AMP: Remote assistive communication and hardware abstraction precede AMP.

Paper: Publish-Subscribe Architecture for Delivering Assistance to Visually Impaired People
Research Problem: Remote assistance to visually impaired users
Major Findings: Uses MQTT to connect assistance consumers and providers.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; detailed delivery lifecycle not verified.
Relevance to AMP: MQTT-based assistive routing is established.

Paper: Bidirectional Braille-speech Communication System for Deafblind Students
Venue: Journal on Efficiency and Responsibility in Education and Science
System / Method: Bidirectional prototype with tactile output and speech processing
Human Evaluation?: Yes; surrogate evaluation, not Deafblind users
Major Findings: Demonstrates conversion and prototype trials.
Limitations: No Deafblind participants: sighted/hearing trials and simulated impairment. Alternating use and surface contact constrain interaction.
Relevance to AMP: Bidirectional Braille–speech conversion is prior art; target-user effectiveness is not demonstrated here.

Paper: AACrobat: Using Mobile Devices to Lower Communication Barriers and Provide Autonomy with Gaze-Based AAC
Venue: Proceedings of the 2017 ACM Conference on Computer Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing
Research Problem: Autonomy and partner assistance in gaze AAC
System / Method: AACrobat: gaze device and mobile companion linked through cloud data
Capability Awareness?: User controls; no general capability handshake verified
Presentation Tracking?: Typing/speaking status; not durable render checkpoints
Major Findings: Supports user-controlled partner collaboration and visibility into communication state.
Limitations: Studied primarily co-located; distributed implementation does not establish remote conversational effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: AAC already includes distributed heterogeneous devices, preferences and conversation state.

Paper: Vibration-based communication for deafblind people
Presentation Tracking?: User playback controls; not delivery lifecycle
Major Findings: Explores customizable local communication with Deafblind users.
Limitations: Remote networked protocol not evaluated; usability varies. Replay requests do not establish automatic crash recovery.
Relevance to AMP: Accessible pacing, customization and replay needs have assistive precedents.

Paper: SymbolChat: A flexible picture-based communication platform for users with intellectual disabilities
Research Problem: Communication access for people with intellectual disabilities
Major Findings: Describes remote messaging adapted to individual needs.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; wire protocol and recovery not verified.
Relevance to AMP: Remote accessible messaging and interface adaptation predate AMP.

Paper: Remote communication for people with disabilities: Support persons’ views on benefits, challenges, and suggestions for technology development
Research Problem: Benefits and barriers of remote communication
Major Findings: Finds social and practical support needs alongside technology barriers.
Limitations: Support-person accounts are proxy evidence, not protocol benchmarks.
Relevance to AMP: Communication success depends on support and access conditions.

Paper: Augmentative and Alternative Communication and digital participation
Major Findings: Connects communication access to digital participation.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; not an evaluated new protocol.
Relevance to AMP: AAC participation motivates requirements beyond device connection.

Paper: A Systematic Review of Ability-diverse Collaboration through Ability-based Lens in HCI
Venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
System / Method: Systematic literature review using an ability-based lens
Major Findings: Synthesizes how abilities and collaboration are represented in HCI.
Limitations: Its reviewed corpus is not the search corpus of this dossier.
Relevance to AMP: Mixed-ability collaboration is an established research field.

Paper: Understanding How Accessibility Practices Impact Teamwork in Mixed-Ability Teams that Collaborate Virtually
Venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
Research Problem: Accessibility practices in virtual mixed-ability teams
Major Findings: Examines how accessibility practices affect teamwork.
Limitations: Qualitative contextual evidence, not controlled transport evaluation.
Relevance to AMP: User agency and team practices must inform AMP preference controls.

Paper: Accessibility-Driven Information Transformations in Mixed-Visual Ability Work Teams
Venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
Major Findings: Examines transformation work within collaborative teams.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; no protocol performance inferred.
Relevance to AMP: Cross-modal conversion can entail human work and access tradeoffs.

Paper: Designing for Collective Access: In Search of a Solution to Accessible Communication in a Mixed-Ability Non-Profit
Venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Designing Interactive Systems Conference
Research Problem: Conflicting access needs in mixed-ability communication
System / Method: Interviews and field observations in a nonprofit
Major Findings: Shows that conflicting access needs involve social roles, norms and accountability.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; not a protocol comparison. Author manuscript and published DOI identify the same work.
Relevance to AMP: Fallback selection cannot assume one universally preferred modality.

Paper: Integrating IoT platforms using the INTER-IoT approach: A case study of the CasAware project
Venue: Journal of Ambient Intelligence and Smart Environments
Major Findings: Combines platform bridges with semantic mediation in an assisted-living case.
Limitations: Assisted-living integration is not person-to-person accessible presentation.
Relevance to AMP: IoT syntactic and semantic interoperability are prior art.

Paper: Towards a new semantic middleware for service description, discovery, selection, and composition in the Internet of Things
System / Method: Semantic middleware for description, discovery, selection and composition
Major Findings: Describes context-aware semantic service orchestration.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; accessible output lifecycle not verified.
Relevance to AMP: Semantic discovery and composition are not AMP novelty.

Paper: A comparative study of systems for the design of flexible user interfaces
Venue: Journal of Ambient Intelligence and Smart Environments
System / Method: Comparative analysis including URC and GPII
Major Findings: Describes reusable interface and preference infrastructure.
Limitations: Comparison of frameworks; not AMP-style conversational recovery experiments.
Relevance to AMP: Device-independent interfaces and preference infrastructure are established.

Paper: A Multilayer Architecture towards the Development and Distribution of Multimodal Interface Applications on the Edge
Research Problem: Distribution of multimodal applications at the edge
Major Findings: Describes edge deployment and remote management, including assisted-living demonstration.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; human evaluation and reliability guarantees not verified.
Relevance to AMP: Assistive edge multimodal architecture is prior art.

Paper: CLAID: Closing the Loop on AI & Data Collection — A cross-platform transparent computing middleware framework for smart edge-cloud and digital biomarker applications
Major Findings: Supports integration across platforms and distributed computation.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; digital biomarker focus, not accessible conversation.
Relevance to AMP: Edge distribution and platform bridging are implementation foundations.

Paper: A Cloud Robotics Platform to Enable Remote Communication for Deafblind People
Venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science; Computers Helping People with Special Needs
System / Method: Cloud robotics with tracking and robotic output
Major Findings: Extends a cloud-robotics direction for remote communication.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; related to PARLOMA, not independent replication.
Relevance to AMP: Cloud-based remote tactile communication precedes AMP.

Paper: Teleintervention for users of augmentative and alternative communication devices: A systematic review
Major Findings: Reviews delivery of AAC intervention at a distance.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; intervention delivery differs from peer messaging interoperability.
Relevance to AMP: Remote AAC literature is relevant but not automatically equivalent to an assistive protocol.

Paper: Promote Assistive and AAC technologies during Covid-19
Venue: Form@re - Open Journal per la formazione in rete
Major Findings: Discusses access through assistive technologies during pandemic restrictions.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; no new transport or recovery contract.
Relevance to AMP: Gaze-based remote participation is not an unexplored application.

Paper: Communicating with Humans and Robots: A Motion Tracking Data Glove for Enhanced Support of Deafblind
Venue: Proceedings of the Annual Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences; Proceedings of the 55th Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences
Research Problem: Communication and robot interaction for Deafblind users
System / Method: Motion-tracking data glove using an extended Malossi approach
Major Findings: Describes a glove supporting communication and interaction.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; no detailed evaluation result inferred. Author names match Crossref and the official AIS proceedings listing.
Relevance to AMP: Glove-mediated remote assistive communication is relevant prior art.

Paper: Lightweight Asynchronous Snapshots for Distributed Dataflows
System / Method: Asynchronous Barrier Snapshotting on Apache Flink
Major Findings: Checkpoint recovery of computation is established; physical presentation is a different boundary.
Limitations: Digital operator recovery is not evidence of exactly-once human perception.
Relevance to AMP: Checkpoint recovery of computation is established; physical presentation is a different boundary.

Paper: Better never than late: meeting deadlines in datacenter networks
Venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGCOMM 2011 conference
Major Findings: Investigates deadline-aware resource allocation.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; datacenter conditions differ from assistive output queues.
Relevance to AMP: Deadline awareness alone is established; AMP needs an application-specific advantage.

Paper: IoT Middleware: A Survey on Issues and Enabling technologies
System / Method: Survey of middleware and enabling technologies
Major Findings: Organizes middleware concerns including integration and adaptation.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only. Crossref early-access metadata has a conflicting author name and provisional pages.
Relevance to AMP: IoT middleware is a mature comparison domain for AMP.

Paper: What are Multimodalities Made of? Modeling Output in a Multimodal Dialogue System
Peer Reviewed?: Workshop publication; review procedure not verified
Major Findings: Multimodal output systems already used acknowledgments after completed presentation.
Limitations: Not evidence of durable cross-device partial-presentation recovery in assistive conversation.
Relevance to AMP: Multimodal output systems already used acknowledgments after completed presentation.

Paper: Mediated and non-mediated tactile fingerspelling: a comparative study
Major Findings: Device-mediated letters were harder to decipher than human-articulated letters, with differences by tactile site.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; participant access characteristics and detailed methods not verified.
Relevance to AMP: Renderer actuation and intelligibility must be evaluated separately.

Paper: Multimodal Architecture and Interfaces
Major Findings: Distributed modality components and start/done/pause/resume lifecycle are established.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Distributed modality components and start/done/pause/resume lifecycle are established.

Paper: Multimodal Interaction Framework
System / Method: Recognition, interpretation, generation, presentation and session functions
Major Findings: Modality separation, user/context adaptation and session concepts predate AMP.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Modality separation, user/context adaptation and session concepts predate AMP.

Paper: EMMA: Extensible MultiModal Annotation markup language
System / Method: XML annotations including confidence and timing
Major Findings: Intermediate interpretation exchange is established; EMMA is not a universal meaning-preserving translator.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Intermediate interpretation exchange is established; EMMA is not a universal meaning-preserving translator.

Paper: Web of Things (WoT) Thing Description 1.1
System / Method: Properties, actions, events, data schemas and security descriptions
Major Findings: Device/service description has an existing standard foundation.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Device/service description has an existing standard foundation.

Paper: Web of Things (WoT) Discovery
Major Findings: Discovery infrastructure should be reused or compared, not renamed as AMP novelty.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Discovery infrastructure should be reused or compared, not renamed as AMP novelty.

Paper: MQTT Version 5.0
System / Method: QoS, sessions, expiry and receive limits
Flow Control / Pacing?: Receive Maximum limits in-flight QoS packets
Major Findings: MQTT acknowledgment concerns protocol delivery, not proof of accessible presentation.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: MQTT acknowledgment concerns protocol delivery, not proof of accessible presentation.

Paper: Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) Version 1.0
System / Method: Link credit, settlement, delivery states and link recovery
Major Findings: Receiver credit and partial-transfer resume are prior art; transfer offsets do not establish tactile progress.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Receiver credit and partial-transfer resume are prior art; transfer offsets do not establish tactile progress.

Paper: Reactive Streams for the JVM, version 1.0.4
Research Problem: Preventing fast producers overwhelming slow consumers
Major Findings: Receiver-demand backpressure is established; specification does not define assistive meaning.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Receiver-demand backpressure is established; specification does not define assistive meaning.

Paper: XEP-0333: Displayed Markers, version 1.0.0
Presentation Tracking?: Yes; displayed marker, not verified comprehension
Major Findings: Displayed state differs from receipt; the specification also requires accessible marker representations and privacy controls.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Displayed state differs from receipt; the specification also requires accessible marker representations and privacy controls.

Paper: XEP-0198: Stream Management, version 1.6.3
Major Findings: Session resumption and transport/application boundary management precede AMP.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Session resumption and transport/application boundary management precede AMP.

Paper: Bundle Protocol Version 7 (RFC 9171)
System / Method: Bundles, lifetime, fragmentation and status reports
Major Findings: Intermittency, expiry and durable forwarding are established; presentation needs an additional contract.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Intermittency, expiry and durable forwarding are established; presentation needs an additional contract.

Paper: Framework for Real-Time Text over IP Using the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) (RFC 5194)
Major Findings: Accessible remote multimedia and relay architectures are prior art.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Accessible remote multimedia and relay architectures are prior art.

Paper: T.140 Real-Time Text Conversation over WebRTC Data Channels (RFC 8865)
System / Method: T.140 data channels and SDP negotiation
Major Findings: Receiver maximum character rate can be negotiated and updated; overflow handling is explicit.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Receiver maximum character rate can be negotiated and updated; overflow handling is explicit.

Paper: Negotiating Human Language in Real-Time Communications (RFC 8373)
Research Problem: Language needs and preferences in sessions
System / Method: SDP language negotiation per medium and direction
Major Findings: Language preferences and directional negotiation are established; language-based routing and UI are outside this RFC.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Language preferences and directional negotiation are established; language-based routing and UI are outside this RFC.

Paper: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) (RFC 9293)
Major Findings: Receiver window flow control is established and operates below accessible presentation.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Receiver window flow control is established and operates below accessible presentation.

Paper: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
System / Method: Success criteria including timing and interaction controls
Major Findings: Timing and control requirements inform interfaces; WCAG is not a complete assistive hardware or protocol standard.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Timing and control requirements inform interfaces; WCAG is not a complete assistive hardware or protocol standard.

Paper: ISO/IEC 24752-1:2014 — Universal remote console — Part 1: General framework
Research Problem: Accessible and replaceable remote user interfaces
Major Findings: Pluggable, device-independent remote interfaces are older prior art.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only. Withdrawn edition is historical prior art, not a recommendation to implement a current standard.
Relevance to AMP: Pluggable, device-independent remote interfaces are older prior art.

Paper: ISO/IEC 24751-2:2008 — Individualized adaptability and accessibility in e-learning, education and training — Part 2: Access for all personal needs and preferences for digital delivery
System / Method: Functional preference representation for digital delivery
Major Findings: Preference-based access matching is established independently of diagnosis labels.
Limitations: Assessment based on abstract only; education/digital-delivery scope, not an AMP session implementation.
Relevance to AMP: Preference-based access matching is established independently of diagnosis labels.

Paper: XEP-0184: Message Delivery Receipts, version 1.4.0
Major Findings: Receipt at a recipient client does not imply reading or understanding.
Limitations: Specification defines functionality; not evidence of AMP effectiveness.
Relevance to AMP: Receipt at a recipient client does not imply reading or understanding.

Paper: XEP-0085: Chat State Notifications, version 2.1
System / Method: Active, composing, paused, inactive and gone states
